title: test(ci-cd-doc): read the Playwright reporter through the shared comment mask
body:
Fixes #9613

## What this changes

`reporterValueOf` in `scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` hand-rolled a two-regex TypeScript comment stripper — a block-comment regex plus a `//`-to-end-of-line rule carrying an ad-hoc one-character guard so the `:` in a URL would save it — under a docblock that argued, correctly, why a whole-file regex is wrong for this input. It now calls `stripComments` from `scripts/js-comment-mask.mjs`, this tree's one answer to "is this span a comment, or code?". The prose and the code agree afterwards; the paragraph that argued the case is kept and the sentence that described the regex is gone.

`stripComments` and not `maskComments` because this reader reports neither a line number nor a byte offset — it returns a captured value — which is the module's own stated rule for choosing between its two projections.

## The mis-mask was MEASURED, and it is latent

The card was graded p2 because nobody had produced an input the regex gets wrong. Measured before the swap, on `playwright.live.config.ts` as it stands: the two strippers agree **byte for byte**.

| reading | naive two-regex stripper | `js-comment-mask.mjs` |
| --- | --- | --- |
| comment bytes | 1,779 | 1,779 |
| characters one calls prose and the other calls code | 0 | 0 |
| characters one calls code and the other calls prose | 0 | 0 |
| `reporterValueOf` answer | `[['list']]` | `[['list']]` |

The population checked was the whole 61-line file, not a sample: every line holding a `//` (four — three `http://` URLs, all behind a `:`, and the real line comment beside `SELF_DEPTH_BELOW_REPO_ROOT`, which is the only one the naive rule fires on); every string literal holding a `/` (seven); every string literal holding a block-comment opener or terminator (none); every regex literal (none).

**So: the current file contains no construct the naive regex mis-handles. The finding is latent, not live**, and the reporter value this file feeds the four #8238 claim sites was never wrong. The file does hold the trigger SHAPE the masker's header names — a URL inside a string, in live code — and survives it only because of that one-character `:` guard, which is a patch over the defect rather than an answer to it.

## The pin, and it is red for the reason it names

The new case pins the shape the config does not hold today and a Playwright config plausibly grows tomorrow: `testIgnore` and `testMatch` take globs, and a glob spells a block-comment opener inside a string. The regex opens a comment there and runs to the next real terminator — a docblock BELOW `reporter:` — swallowing the reporter line. The reader then answers `undefined`, which trips the vacuity leg into reporting that the config no longer declares a reporter at all: a false alarm pointing at a config that is fine.

Ablation, run from the committed fix, with the mutation proven on disk before the run (`stripComments(source)` count 1 to 0, naive rule 0 to 1, blob hash changed) and restored with `git checkout HEAD -- path` verified by an empty `git diff HEAD`:

- **mutated (naive stripper back):** `Tests 1 failed | 84 passed (85)`, the single failure being the new case — `AssertionError: expected undefined to be '[['list']]'`, in 11ms, so not a timeout.
- **as landed:** `Tests 85 passed (85)`.

**The control, reasoned before it was read:** the other 84 cases must NOT move, because every one of them reads a real file and the measurement above says the two strippers give identical answers on the real file — `playwright.live.config.ts` is not in this diff and neither is `live-e2e.yml`. Specifically, `declaresHtmlReporter` stays false and `globsReport` stays false, so `uploads no path the reporter cannot produce` keeps taking the same branch. They did not move: 84 passed in both legs. A count that moved would have meant the swap changed an answer somewhere, which is the thing this change may not do.

⛔ Not asserted anywhere: a grep count of the retired function name. It would have read 1 to 0 in code while the family it belonged to is still named in prose, which is a number that cannot distinguish the two.

## How it escaped, which is the reusable half

objectui#9183 moved 29 source-scanning carriers onto the shared mask. Its changeset rules three carriers out, verbatim: "their stripper is not applied to JavaScript: ... `ci-cd-pipeline-doc` strips Markdown and YAML". That is true of the FILE and false of this SITE inside it — the same file also holds a TypeScript stripper, and the census never looked past the file. ⭐ **A census keyed on which FILE holds a stripper cannot see a second stripper in a MIXED file, and an explicit pass and an unseen site read identically afterwards.** That sentence is now carried in `reporterValueOf`'s docblock, which is the only place a future reader of this call site will look.

## Gates run before pushing — the whole-class population, not only the ones naming this path

| gate | population | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `pnpm check:comment-mask-corpus` | every source file in the tree | exit 0 — 5,055 files, 1 disagreement, 0 fabricated bytes, 1,517 over-masked; unchanged residue, still only `apps/console/src/pages/DocsIndex.tsx` |
| `pnpm check:control-bytes` | all files | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:test-path-roots` | all test sources | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:pending-changeset-literals` | all files | exit 0 |
| `pnpm check:new-line-citations` | the diff against the base | exit 0 — 0 new citations |
| `pnpm check:esm-specifiers` | published ESM packages | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-lint-coverage.mjs` | all packages | exit 0 — 46/46 linted |
| `pnpm check:lint-rule-coverage` | all tracked source | exit 0 |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | the diff | exit 0 — nothing published moved, no changeset owed |
| 11 population tests | all markdown readers, all test sources, the runner environment, the masker's own corpus | exit 0 — 340 tests |

The corpus gate was the one most likely to object, and it was run rather than reasoned about: this diff puts a block-comment opener AND a terminator inside string literals in a test source, which is exactly the shape that family gets wrong. The masker handles both — the sweep's disagreement count did not move.

The 11 population tests are `markdown-test-inputs`, `check-test-path-roots`, `one-authority-per-exported-name-6273`, `vitest-invocation-guard`, `js-comment-mask-jsx-6891`, `js-comment-mask-param-types-9324`, `check-comment-mask-corpus`, `check-vi-mock-specifiers`, `check-vi-mock-inherit`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape`, `network-escape-ledger`.

Direct checks: `pnpm exec vitest run scripts/__tests__/ci-cd-pipeline-doc.test.ts` — 85 passed. `pnpm type-check:scripts` — exit 0, and `tsc --listFiles` confirms BOTH the edited test and `js-comment-mask.mjs` are inside that project, so the typecheck is not excluding what it is claimed to cover. `pnpm exec eslint --format json` over the changed file — 1 file judged, 0 errors, 0 warnings, not ignored; `eslint.config.js` declares no `projectService` and no `parserOptions.project`, so linting here is not type-aware and a one-file diff cannot move the verdict of any untouched file. CI's `pnpm lint` is `turbo run lint` over the 46 packages, and `scripts/` is not a package, so this run is strictly more than CI opens for this path.

## NOT MEASURED

`pnpm check:node-esm-load` exits 1 in this container, and the reason is environmental rather than this diff: turbo shares one cache across every worktree of the checkout, and the provenance leg refused two entries — `@object-ui/auth` and `@object-ui/react-runtime` — because they were replayed from a sibling agent's worktree. 35 of 37 gradable entries were built by this tree and none was faulted. This diff adds no published package source and no ESM specifier, so the gate is uncoupled to it; the specifier half of the same script (`pnpm check:esm-specifiers`) passed. Re-reading it cleanly needs a forced rebuild of 45 packages, which would repopulate the shared cache underneath the other agents in this container. Declared rather than taken.

## Acceptance notes

Scope was the declared surface: `scripts/` and `scripts/__tests__/`. One file changed.

**Not fixed here, reported instead — the census-classification carrier has no home inside this surface.** A ledger that classified by SITE rather than by FILE would be the durable fix for the escape above. A gate at `scripts/check-*.mjs` would be path-wise inside the declared surface, but its findings are not: measured on this branch, four more carriers still hand-roll a naive stripper after objectui#9183, and all four live under `packages/`. Landing that gate here would either turn the tree red over files this PR may not touch, or ship with a baseline that grows — which `check-comment-mask-corpus.mjs`'s own header names as the wrong remedy for exactly this class. It wants its own card.

Reproduction, from the repo root:

    git grep -nE "replace\(/..\*\[..s..S\]\*\?..\*..//g" -- 'packages/**/*.ts' 'packages/**/*.tsx'

The four sites, and what they are:

- `packages/types/src/__tests__/overlay-node-slot-doc-types-7082.test.ts`
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/alert-dialog-read-dialect-7104.test.ts`
- `packages/types/src/__tests__/overlay-trigger-union-7081.test.ts`
- `packages/plugin-form/src/LineItemsPanel.parentIdNoCast-9333.test.ts`

Two of them were measured against their own subjects the same way this card's site was — `overlay-node-slot-doc-types-7082` over `packages/types/src/overlay.ts` (52,424 bytes) and `LineItemsPanel.parentIdNoCast-9333` over `packages/plugin-form/src/LineItemsPanel.tsx` (15,901 bytes). Both agree with the shared mask byte for byte today, so all of these are latent too, exactly like this one. ⭐ The load-bearing detail is not the damage — there is none today — it is that objectui#9333 landed a NEW naive stripper AFTER objectui#9183 swept the tree. The class recurs, and nothing in CI can see it recur.

Noted, not filed: `canonical()` in `scripts/check-doc-example-shared-reader.mjs` applies the same block-comment regex, but to a single AST node's text rather than to a whole file, which bounds the phantom to one expression. Carrier: this PR's acceptance notes. Named because the next person to sweep for that regex will hit it and should not have to re-derive that it is a different risk.

## Landing

Draft, and it stays draft — this seat neither flips it ready, enables auto-merge, nor requests review.
